Name: Medical Stop-Loss Captive
Also Known As: Group stop-loss captive; Employer stop-loss captive
Plain-English Description: Lets several self-funded employers share a layer of stop-loss risk through a captive, with an insurer covering the very large claims above that layer.
Example: Forty mid-sized employers pool the first $250,000 of each large claim above their deductibles in a captive and share any surplus.
Full Path: Health Insurance > Major Medical (Comprehensive) > Employer Group Health > Medical Stop-Loss > Medical Stop-Loss Captive

Name: Organ Transplant Carve-Out
Also Known As: Transplant stop-loss; Transplant coverage
Plain-English Description: Moves the cost of covered organ transplants out of a self-funded health plan to an insurer, alongside the plan's regular stop-loss.
Example: An employee needs a liver transplant and the transplant policy pays the hospital bills instead of the employer's plan.
Full Path: Health Insurance > Major Medical (Comprehensive) > Employer Group Health > Medical Stop-Loss > Organ Transplant Carve-Out

Name: Cell & Gene Therapy Carve-Out
Also Known As: CGT stop-loss; Gene therapy coverage
Plain-English Description: Insures a health plan against the very high one-off cost of approved cell and gene therapies.
Example: A child on an employer plan receives a gene therapy costing about $2 million and the carve-out policy pays it.
US Notes: Separately, CMS runs a Cell and Gene Therapy Access Model for Medicaid sickle cell gene therapies; 33 states plus DC and Puerto Rico signed up (2025).
Full Path: Health Insurance > Major Medical (Comprehensive) > Employer Group Health > Medical Stop-Loss > Cell & Gene Therapy Carve-Out

Name: Multiemployer (Taft-Hartley) Health Plan
Also Known As: Taft-Hartley plan; Union health and welfare fund
Plain-English Description: A health plan run by a union trust that covers workers of many employers under a collective bargaining agreement, often self-funded with stop-loss.
Example: Construction workers who move between contractors keep coverage through their union's health fund.
US Notes: Set up under section 302(c)(5) of the Labor Management Relations Act of 1947, which requires a written trust run by equal numbers of employer and union trustees.
Full Path: Health Insurance > Major Medical (Comprehensive) > Employer Group Health > Multiemployer (Taft-Hartley) Health Plan

Name: Group Medical Gap Insurance
Also Known As: Gap plan; Deductible reimbursement plan
Plain-English Description: Employer-paid supplemental cover that pays part of the deductible and coinsurance left by the group major medical plan.
Example: An employee's $3,000 hospital deductible is mostly paid by the gap plan directly to the hospital.
Full Path: Health Insurance > Supplemental Health (Voluntary Benefits) > Group Medical Gap Insurance

Name: High-Limit Disability Insurance
Also Known As: Excess disability; Jumbo disability
Plain-English Description: Disability cover for high earners whose income is above the most that standard disability insurers will cover.
Example: A surgeon earning $1.5 million a year buys extra monthly disability benefits on top of her regular policy.
US Notes: Usually written in the surplus lines market, most often at Lloyd's; California's surplus lines export list includes 'high limits disability' above admitted issue and participation limits.
Full Path: Health Insurance > Disability Insurance > High-Limit Disability Insurance

Name: Key Person Disability
Also Known As: Key man disability; Contingent personal accident
Plain-English Description: Pays a business if an essential owner, executive or star performer is disabled and the business loses revenue or must find a replacement.
Example: A software firm receives a lump sum to hire a new CTO after its founder is disabled in a car crash.
Full Path: Health Insurance > Disability Insurance > Key Person Disability

Name: Contractors Professional Liability
Also Known As: Contractors E&O; Design-build professional liability
Plain-English Description: Covers contractors for mistakes in design and other professional services they provide or subcontract, which a CGL policy does not cover.
Example: A design-build contractor is sued after its engineered roof design fails and must be rebuilt.
Full Path: Specialty Insurance > Professional Liability (E&O) > Contractors Professional Liability

Name: Medical Billing E&O
Also Known As: Billing errors and omissions; Regulatory billing E&O
Plain-English Description: Covers medical billers and healthcare providers for coding and billing mistakes, including the cost of defending billing audits by government or private payers.
Example: A billing company submits claims to the wrong insurer and the clinic sues it for lost revenue.
Full Path: Specialty Insurance > Professional Liability (E&O) > Medical Billing E&O

Name: Over-Redemption Insurance
Also Known As: Promotional risk insurance; Coupon redemption insurance
Plain-English Description: Pays a marketer's extra costs if a coupon, rebate or money-back offer is claimed by far more customers than expected.
Example: A rebate offer expected to be claimed by 5% of buyers is claimed by 20% and the insurer pays the excess.
Full Path: Specialty Insurance > Event & Entertainment Insurance > Over-Redemption Insurance

Name: Weather Promotion Insurance
Also Known As: Promotional weather insurance; Rain-back promotion
Plain-English Description: Pays a retailer back for refunds it promised customers if a named weather event happens on a set date.
Example: A jeweler promises full refunds if it snows 3 inches on New Year's Day; it snows and the insurer pays the refunds.
Full Path: Specialty Insurance > Weather Insurance > Weather Promotion Insurance

Name: Contractual Bonus Insurance
Also Known As: Performance bonus insurance
Plain-English Description: Pays a team, sponsor or studio the bonus it owes an athlete or entertainer who hits a performance target in their contract.
Example: A team owes its quarterback a $1 million bonus for reaching the playoffs and the policy pays it.
Full Path: Specialty Insurance > Sports & Contingency > Contractual Bonus Insurance

Name: Amateur Sports Insurance
Also Known As: Youth sports insurance; League insurance
Plain-English Description: Package of liability and participant accident cover for amateur teams, leagues, camps and clubs.
Example: A youth soccer league buys cover for coaches, volunteers and players' accident medical bills.
Full Path: Specialty Insurance > Sports & Contingency > Amateur Sports Insurance

Name: Tenant User Liability (TULIP)
Also Known As: Tenant user liability insurance policy; Facility user liability
Plain-English Description: A venue's own program that lets people who rent its space buy the event liability cover the venue requires.
Example: A couple renting a town hall for a wedding buys liability cover through the hall's online link.
Full Path: Casualty & Liability Insurance > Specialty Casualty Lines > Special Event Liability > Tenant User Liability (TULIP)

Name: Game Promotion (Sweepstakes) Bond
Also Known As: Sweepstakes bond; Game of chance bond
Plain-English Description: A surety bond a sweepstakes or contest sponsor files with a state to guarantee the promised prizes will be awarded.
Example: A soft drink brand runs a $50,000 sweepstakes and files a bond in Florida before launch.
US Notes: Florida (Fla. Stat. 849.094) requires a trust account, surety bond or waiver for game promotions with prizes over $5,000; New York also requires bonding and registration over $5,000, and Rhode Island requires registration only (over $500).
Full Path: Financial Lines > Surety Bonds > Commercial Surety > Game Promotion (Sweepstakes) Bond

Name: Oil & Gas Bonds
Also Known As: Plugging and abandonment bonds; Decommissioning bonds; Lease bonds
Plain-English Description: Surety bonds that guarantee energy operators will meet lease duties such as plugging wells and removing platforms.
Example: An offshore operator posts a bond so the government is not left paying to remove its platform.
US Notes: Offshore, BOEM requires base lease bonds and may require supplemental financial assurance for decommissioning (30 CFR Part 556, Subpart I).
Full Path: Financial Lines > Surety Bonds > Commercial Surety > Oil & Gas Bonds

Name: Non-Trade Credit Insurance
Also Known As: Lender non-payment insurance; Bank credit insurance
Plain-English Description: Protects banks and other lenders if a borrower fails to repay a loan or trade-finance facility.
Example: A bank insures 80% of a loan to a foreign company so it can lend more within its risk limits.
Full Path: Financial Lines > Credit Insurance > Non-Trade Credit Insurance

Name: Sovereign Non-Payment
Also Known As: Public buyer default; Non-honoring of sovereign financial obligations
Plain-English Description: Covers exporters and lenders when a government or state-owned buyer fails to pay what it owes.
Example: A state-owned utility abroad fails to pay a US equipment maker for delivered turbines.
Full Path: Specialty Insurance > Political Risk Insurance (PRI) > Sovereign Non-Payment

Name: Active Assailant Insurance
Also Known As: Active shooter insurance; Deadly weapon protection
Plain-English Description: Covers costs after an attack with a gun, knife, vehicle or other weapon, such as crisis response, victim support, business interruption and legal liability.
Example: After a shooting at a shopping center, the policy pays for counseling, security upgrades and lost rent.
Full Path: Specialty Insurance > Active Assailant Insurance

Name: Maritime Piracy (Marine K&R)
Also Known As: Piracy insurance; Marine kidnap and ransom
Plain-English Description: Covers ransom and related costs when a ship or its crew is seized by pirates.
Example: Pirates hold a cargo ship off East Africa and the policy pays the ransom and crisis consultants.
US Notes: Paying ransom to sanctioned persons is prohibited by OFAC.
Full Path: Specialty Insurance > Kidnap, Ransom & Extortion (K&R) > Maritime Piracy (Marine K&R)

Name: Sexual Abuse & Molestation Liability
Also Known As: SAM liability; Sexual misconduct and molestation (SML)
Plain-English Description: Covers organizations against claims of sexual abuse by staff or volunteers, including claims of negligent hiring or supervision, which most CGL policies exclude.
Example: A youth camp is sued for failing to supervise a counselor accused of abuse.
Full Path: Casualty & Liability Insurance > Specialty Casualty Lines > Sexual Abuse & Molestation Liability

Name: Tenant Discrimination Liability
Also Known As: Fair housing liability
Plain-English Description: Covers landlords and property managers against claims that they discriminated against current, past or would-be tenants.
Example: An applicant who uses a wheelchair says an apartment manager refused to rent to her.
US Notes: Housing discrimination is barred by the federal Fair Housing Act (42 U.S.C. 3601 and following) and state and local laws.
Full Path: Casualty & Liability Insurance > Specialty Casualty Lines > Tenant Discrimination Liability

Name: Energy Insurance
Also Known As: Oil and gas insurance; Energy package
Plain-English Description: Specialist property, liability and well-control cover for oil, gas and power businesses, onshore and offshore.
Example: An offshore oil producer insures its platform, pipelines and the cost of regaining control of a well.
US Notes: Offshore facilities must show oil spill financial responsibility under OPA 90 (30 CFR Part 553), starting at $35 million; insurance is one accepted method.
Full Path: Commercial Lines (Business Property & Packages) > Energy Insurance

Name: Control of Well
Also Known As: Operator's extra expense (OEE); Well control insurance
Plain-English Description: Pays to regain control of a blown-out oil or gas well, plus re-drilling and pollution clean-up costs.
Example: A gas well blows out during drilling and the policy pays the well-control specialists.
Full Path: Commercial Lines (Business Property & Packages) > Energy Insurance > Control of Well

Name: Renewable Energy Insurance
Also Known As: Renewables insurance; Wind and solar insurance
Plain-English Description: Covers wind, solar, battery and other clean-energy projects against damage, breakdown, lost revenue and liability during building and operation.
Example: Hail smashes panels at a solar farm and the policy pays for repairs and lost power sales.
Full Path: Commercial Lines (Business Property & Packages) > Energy Insurance > Renewable Energy Insurance

Name: Public Entity Insurance
Also Known As: Municipal insurance; Public entity package
Plain-English Description: Package of property, liability, auto and management cover designed for towns, counties, school and water districts and other local governments.
Example: A township insures its town hall, snowplows, police liability and officials under one program.
US Notes: AGRiP estimates at least 80% of US local public entities belong to one or more public entity risk pools instead of, or as well as, buying commercial insurance.
Full Path: Commercial Lines (Business Property & Packages) > Business Package Policies > Public Entity Insurance

Name: Public Officials Liability
Also Known As: Public officials E&O; POL
Plain-English Description: Covers elected and appointed officials and their public body for claims over decisions they make in office.
Example: A zoning board is sued by a developer after it denies a building permit.
Full Path: Specialty Insurance > Management Liability > Public Officials Liability

Name: Residual Value Insurance
Also Known As: Residual value guarantee (RVG); RVI
Plain-English Description: Guarantees that an asset such as a plane, vehicle or building will be worth at least an agreed amount on a future date, paying the shortfall if it is worth less.
Example: A lessor insures that a leased jet will be worth $20 million at lease end and is paid the difference when it sells for $16 million.
Full Path: Financial Lines > Residual Value Insurance
